facts.timeline_arc: Mid‑2025 Nestle faced legal challenges and a leadership transition, with lawsuits over ultra‑processed foods and child‑labour allegations. The situation escalated in September when the CEO was removed over a misconduct scandal and shareholders demanded the chairman’s resignation, prompting a wave of cost‑cutting measures including a 16,000‑job layoff in October. Throughout late 2025 and early 2026 the company confronted mounting regulatory pressure, culminating in a San Francisco lawsuit and a high‑profile infant‑formula recall that spread to Europe. Supply‑chain disruptions in March and a surprising profit surge in April highlighted both operational vulnerabilities and resilience. By May the focus returned to safety concerns as a toxin was traced to a Chinese supplier, signaling continued scrutiny of Nestle’s product safety and supply‑chain practices.

turning_points.why: CEO Laurent Freixe was ousted after a whistleblower report, and major shareholders called for the chairman’s resignation, creating leadership turmoil.
Nestlé announced a global layoff of 16,000 jobs as part of a cost‑cutting drive to revive financial performance.
A recall of infant formula batches over possible cereulide toxin triggered a public apology from the CEO and sparked industry‑wide safety concerns.
A major theft of KitKat bars caused supply‑chain losses and an abrupt CEO departure, intensifying investor unease.
Detection of cereulide toxin in a Chinese ingredient supplier led to renewed scrutiny of Nestlé’s infant‑formula supply chain.

text.summary: Nestlé (SIX: NESN, food and beverages) generated 32,708 articles between 2024-06 and 2026-05, of which 8,197 sit in the top priority bands. Attention over the latest three months was 3,066 articles against 3,395 in the prior three months, a ratio of 0.9. The story changed sharply from mid-2025: a CEO removal in September 2025, a 16,000-job layoff announced in October, and an infant-formula recall in January 2026 that drew in safety and supply-chain scrutiny. A KitKat theft and another CEO departure followed in March 2026, and in May a toxin was traced to a Chinese ingredient supplier. Against this, the company reported solid Q1 sales and a profit surprise in April, and it is launching products such as a pistachio Aero bar. The record therefore combines governance and product-safety pressure with operating and product activity.

text.themes_time: Travel rose from 6.7% in 2021 to 14.9% in 2025, and tourism from 1.7% to 5.4%. Hospitality moved from 2.2% to 4.5%, while economy slipped from 9.0% to 7.1% and food industry from 7.2% to 6.6%. Real estate was close to flat, at 6.3% in 2021 and 6.4% in 2025, retail went from 2.8% to 3.0%, and stock market from 1.8% to 1.0%. Finance stood at 14.5% in 2021 but is not among the listed themes for 2025.

Legal and regulatory is small at 115 articles (0.35%) but extremely negative, with a ratio of 37.33, while Leadership (520 articles, 0.94 late versus early) and Finance (407, 0.8) have held up better. AI is the only lens at about its early level, at 1.01, with 376 articles; Partnerships has 320 articles at 0.59.
text.peers: Nestlé holds 48.9% of the combined coverage of the peer group, ahead of Unilever at 34.6% and Procter & Gamble at 16.5%, though its attention is falling (0.72) while Unilever is flat (1.09) and Procter & Gamble is rising (1.35). Its themes lean heavily to travel at 38.1%, with tourism at 13.8%, food industry at 13.6% and hospitality at 13.2%. Unilever and Procter & Gamble instead show finance (15.2% and 17.9%) and technology (11.3% and 9.0%), and Procter & Gamble's negative-to-positive ratio of 0.34 is above the 0.23 shown for both Nestlé and Unilever.
text.mix: Catalyst events (66) outnumbered risk events (17) in the last six months, alongside 26 earnings events and 36 key-people events. Tone is mostly positive, with 0.23 negative stories per positive across the window, though the recall section stands out at 11.93.
text.events: Recent events include a leadership succession in which a new executive replaces Bernie Stefan, who moves to a global role within the group. The company also announced an integrated operating base in TEDA, the new Aero pistachio sharing bar, and solid Q1 sales across nearly all sectors. A founders' share buy-back from Nestlé was reported, and a dismissed X advertiser-boycott lawsuit appeared in the legal feed.
text.risks: Risk coverage centres on lawsuits, regulatory matters and layoffs, with the recall section at 518 articles (1.36% of company coverage) and a negative-to-positive ratio of 11.93. The recall section's last-third-versus-first figure is 26.0, so this theme has grown markedly, and the CEO section (520 articles, ratio 0.53) shows continuing leadership attention.
text.catalysts: Catalyst types include new products, contracts, M&A, asset acquisitions, job creation and FDA approval. Coffee (886 articles, 2.51%) and acquisition (343 articles, 1.05%) are the catalyst sections, but both are lower later in the window, at 0.59 and 0.61 of their early levels.

The travel entries reflect how coverage is tagged and sit apart from Nestlé's core food business.
text.timeline: In September 2025 the CEO Laurent Freixe was ousted after a whistleblower report and shareholders called for the chairman's resignation, followed by the 16,000-job layoff in October.
